# Assessment: release cadence optimization

**Stage:** assess only. **Decision status:** open for operator feedback. This document does not approve a new task order, relax a dependency, certify C08, or enter analyze, plan, execute, or reflect. The observations below distinguish source, compilation, integration, installed use, and publication.

## Operator goal and observed delivery state

The child goals call for a useful independently releasable increment per hour of **active agent runtime**, with The Boss UI alongside the core capability; production tests and builds at completed shipping boundaries; resource-aware parallel ownership; a measured delivery-optimization role; bounded hourly Compass graph refresh; and feedback stops after all five KBD stages ([goals.md](goals.md)). No hourly target has yet been measured or met by evidence in this child.

The current initiative plan contains 18 dependency-ordered changes. It defaults to sequential execution, places bounded teams at C09, the first feedback-to-issue customer workflow at C10, and studio administration at C14. C18 contains broad compatibility and release evidence ([parent plan](../../plan.md), especially §§ Delivery sequence, C09–C10, C14, C18). The plan explicitly distinguishes implementation, evidence, certification and publication. Its release sequencing has no earlier integrated Boss UI increment for C06–C09. This is a **high-confidence structural reason** that useful installed functionality can lag completed provider code; it is not a measurement of agent speed or proof that every dependency can be reordered.

The parent KBD projection currently reports **7/18 initiative changes implemented**, **9/20 run-scope completions**, no conflicts, and separate evidence/certification/publication fields that remain pending or not tracked ([parent progress](../../progress.json)). These are ledger counts, not user-visible releases. The last release acceptance recorded in this initiative is The Boss **2.2.3 P1**: Windows x64 installation and packaged UAR on port 1906 were operator-confirmed; Mac Apple Silicon had local acceptance. Windows occupied-port fallback was not observed ([P1 receipt](../../c01/p1-acceptance-receipt-2026-09-27.json)). C06 and C07 subsequently recorded local macOS arm64 SurrealKV 3.3.0 integration gates, but each receipt expressly excludes installed Windows/Mac package and release-artifact acceptance ([C06 receipt](../../c06/implementation-receipt-2026-09-27.json), [C07 receipt](../../c07/implementation-receipt-2026-09-28.json)).

For C08, static source reconciliation is not compilation or an integration pass ([C08.1](../../c08/c08-1-static-reconciliation-2026-09-28.md), [C08.2/3](../../c08/c08-23-static-reconciliation-2026-09-28.md)). The prepared service collector has not run and cannot certify channel-source or cross-host behavior ([runbook](../../c08/composed-gate-runbook.md)). A carried-over C08 Cargo command has now ended with exit 101, Rust E0382: `projection_sha256` was moved in `crates/librefang-storage/src/channel_actions/surreal_impl/observers.rs` at line 234 after the loop at 163 (origin at 143). This is an **observed compile failure**, reported from that existing command; this assessment launched no new build or test. C08 remains open. C09's stated dependencies C02/C03/C04/C06 have recorded completion; that does not itself waive C08's open status or certify C09 readiness in every consumer.

The Boss already has an individual-agent UAR settings route at `/settings/uar`, with an administration workspace (`UarAdministrationWorkspace.tsx:159–169, 251–279`), allowlisted adapter (`UarAdministrationAdapter.ts:301–324`), typed IPC schemas (`src/shared/ipc/schemas/prometheus.ts:253–343`), main handlers (`:135–160`), and persisted preference definitions (`target-key-definitions.json:927`, `preferenceSchemas.ts:629`). These are **existing vertical-slice assets**, not team-task administration. At inspected UAR source `b18397a3`, team runtime capabilities remain false. The current Boss main revision `1fe9acff` is newer than convergence's older Boss baseline `48070346`; its unrelated manifest edits must be preserved when consuming later UAR source. The Boss sidecar payload pin `92620d40419d5b55af94e2aef0a0db886aa9aadc` predates C08. This source comparison was supplied by the UI owner; it is not a compiled or installed team capability.

Packaging is also a separate critical path. `scripts/import-uar-sidecar-payloads.cjs:139–178` requires immutable **win32-x64 and darwin-arm64** records from the same UAR source before either installer job can use the imported payloads. The installer jobs themselves publish by platform (`.github/workflows/the-boss-release.yml:87–118, 203–215`), while `scripts/release-preflight.cjs:16–45` freezes source/version/profile. `package.json:29–31, 45–46` and `scripts/release-platforms.cjs:5–19` distinguish a plain Mac ARM build that disables UAR from UAR-enabled release scripts. Therefore a locally produced plain Mac DMG would not prove UAR release readiness. This is a high-confidence code-path distinction, not proof that current installer jobs have run.

| Boundary | Current evidence | Confidence and limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source written | C06/C07 implementation receipts and C08 static source reconciliations. | High for recorded source revisions; C08 source is not a runnable claim. |
| Compiled | C06/C07 gates compiled their pinned source. Latest carried-over C08 Cargo ended E0382, exit 101. | High for those exact commands; no later C08 fix/build is known here. |
| Integrated | C06/C07 passed local real-host UAR/SurrealKV gates. C08 composed product path remains unexecuted. | High for receipt scope; no cross-host or channel-source pass. |
| Installed | The Boss 2.2.3 P1 Windows operator and Apple Silicon local acceptance only. | High as recorded; later initiative capability is not established in installers. |
| Published | P1 release receipt exists. No later C06–C08 published installer acceptance appears in this initiative's cited receipts. | Moderate; this is an initiative-record finding, not a search of every external release system. |

## Cadence and evidence quality

The initiative currently has 169 KBD files and 97 OpenSpec files under its planning root, with separate source, product-task, parent-task, gate, archive and release records. C08, for example, has two source-reconciliation reports plus a prepared runbook while product acceptance remains open. This demonstrates **ledger surface area and duplicate status concepts**, not the time spent maintaining them. A reduction proposal needs a measured task-to-ledger time split and must retain truthful ownership and acceptance boundaries.

The Karpathy session log has **one** recorded progress event, C01.1: task completion timestamp, task identity/class, commit, touched-file list, blocker, next-work text and empty verification ([session log](../../../../../.prometheus/session-log.md)). Its `elapsedHours` is `0.0`, and the paired receipt says shared-memory transport was queued after a `pk` timeout ([progress-memory receipt](../../../../../.prometheus/progress-memory-receipts/d4762e71f176530c69aa45e4248b339e0d0843538ac9f804eda4d8680406fc23.json)). That event proves an event was recorded and appended, **not** active agent minutes, hourly throughput, delivered memory, or customer learning. KBD hook timestamps and Git commit timestamps bound wall-clock events; they cannot be summed into model compute or human work time. No current ledger provides active agent time, blocked/waiting time, critical-path elapsed time, build/gate duration by phase, packaging/publishing time, or time from source completion to installed feedback. The one C07 gate receipt records a 127.87-second final gate and earlier fixture failures; it does not yield the initiative's full verification cost.

There is an observed process conflict worth resolving in later stages. The active `bossfang-stewards` team definitions instruct storage and feature roles to work test-first/TDD (`.agent-team/bossfang-stewards/team.json`, storage and feature steward prompts), and repository `AGENTS.md` includes a cargo-check/test ladder. The operator's current phase-boundary instruction takes precedence for this initiative. The earlier conversation disclosed a Python syntax check and a build before the C08 composed gate runner was ready; those are specific admissions of premature verification, **not a comprehensive audited history**. C07's recorded fixture reruns are also visible, but do not alone prove a systematic test-first pattern. The mini KBD `stageGate` treats analyze as optional in general, so this child's mandatory assess → feedback → analyze → feedback → plan → feedback → execute → feedback → reflect stops need explicit stage control; their enforcement cannot be assumed from the generic gate.

At the observed resource snapshot, approximately 112 GiB of disk was free and `vm_stat` showed no swapouts. The host has 64 GiB RAM and 10 logical CPUs; separate Rust, UI and packaging stacks still contend for shared resources. This snapshot does not establish sustained build capacity and does **not** diagnose out-of-memory as the C08 failure. The UAR worktree initially lacked `compass-out`. A bounded `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=2 compass update . --no-cluster --no-viz --timing` finished with exit 0 in **134.98 seconds**, indexing 8,184 files into 447,259 nodes and 495,392 edges and writing 880,925,944 bytes. It published a **partial** graph after omitting 51 nodes and 74 edges with 43 identity collisions; an exact `AgentInstanceController` search found `controller.rs:62`, `pump.rs:70` and `update.rs:398`. The graph now supports positive source navigation, but is not authoritative for negative lookups. The approximately 135-second cold run and 0.88 GB of writes are measured overhead; they do not predict incremental hourly refresh cost or establish that an hourly cadence has occurred. No graph repair or follow-up refresh was initiated here.

## Goal assessment

| Child goal | Assessment now | What is missing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hourly usable, independently releasable full-stack increment with Boss UI | **NOT MET** | No measured active agent minutes; no C06–C08 installed Boss UI artifact or customer workflow receipt. |
| Tests/builds only at completed shipping boundaries | **PARTIAL** | C06/C07 have bounded local integration receipts, but the admitted early checks and conflicting team guidance need reconciliation; C08 compile is currently failing. |
| Resource-aware concurrent ownership | **PARTIAL** | Separate worktrees and file ownership exist; measured contention/critical path and release overlap are absent. |
| Karpathy-backed optimization role and bottleneck measurement | **NOT MET** | One event with `0.0` elapsed hours cannot attribute time or explain waiting; the role has no approved authority or metric contract. |
| Bounded hourly Compass refresh | **NOT MET** | One update is underway after a missing graph; recurring cadence and useful graph-query evidence are not established. |
| Five stages with operator feedback after each | **PARTIAL** | Child is at assess; later feedback stops remain pending and require explicit guarding. |

## Questions for operator feedback before analysis

1. What is the smallest **customer-usable** increment: a local Boss UI workflow, an installable Windows x64 and Apple Silicon pair, or a published release with installed acceptance on both? Core, UI, IPC, internationalization and persistence appear inseparable for anything presented as a releasable Boss capability. A team-catalog preview/validation slice is only useful if the operator accepts management without execution as a real customer action; a durable task/member board is another candidate, while full team execution depends on claims, mailbox and budget semantics as well as UI/IPC/i18n. None is selected here.
2. Does “one per hour” mean one increment per hour of **active session elapsed time**, **summed active agent minutes**, **critical-path elapsed wall time**, or a target reported against more than one clock? At minimum, track active session elapsed and aggregate agent effort separately before choosing a target; waiting, operator gates, packaging and publication must remain visible rather than disappear from the denominator.
3. Which C09/C10 capability can be demonstrated end to end while C08's live channel-source profile remains unsupported? Which dependency conditions are contracts rather than chronological ordering, and who may approve any reordering?
4. What exact resource envelope should bound concurrent Rust, TypeScript UI, docs and release writers on this host and on native Windows/Mac packaging hosts? What result from the current Compass update would justify a repeated hourly refresh?
5. What evidence should a proposed delivery-optimization observer record: active-agent duration, wait/blocker duration, critical path, gate/build time, rollback/rework, first runnable build, installed release, or customer feedback? Candidate role scope is **observation and cadence advice only**; it would have no authority to add tests, rewrite scope, change phase status or declare acceptance.

Potential directions for later analysis are smaller full-stack release boundaries, explicit provider-to-Boss contracts, measuring parallel ownership against contention, and eliminating duplicate ledger entry without losing source/acceptance truth. None is selected here. Parent C08 remains open; this assessment preserves its product and provider acceptance gaps. Await operator feedback before the next KBD stage.

# Goals — agent-fabric-convergence > release-cadence-optimization

- Target a useful independently releasable increment per hour of active agent runtime with The Boss UI delivered alongside core capability.
- Reserve production tests and builds for completed independently shipping phase boundaries.
- Use resource-aware concurrent agent ownership across Rust, TypeScript UI, documentation and release work.
- Use Karpathy evidence to propose a delivery optimization role and measure bottlenecks without inventing timings.
- Refresh and use Compass code graphs hourly during active work with bounded resource use.
- Follow assess analyze plan execute reflect and wait for operator feedback after each stage; preserve parent work and return point.
